docs.title: CreditShield Documentation
docs.text: CreditShield is a full-stack digital lending platform that automates the 7-stage loan origination lifecycle with AI-powered risk assessment.

docs.title: What CreditShield Does
docs.text:
CreditShield manages loan applications from initial borrower contact through final underwriting decision. The platform combines rule-based policy enforcement with explainable AI analysis to help lenders make faster, more consistent credit decisions while maintaining regulatory compliance.

Key capabilities:

  • 7-stage workflow: Structured loan origination from application intake to post-decision handover
  • 50+ underwriting rules: Automated hard and soft rule evaluation across 5 risk categories
  • AI-powered analysis: AWS Bedrock with Llama 3 70B generates explainable credit decisions
  • 4-page appraisal reports: Bank-grade professional reports for loan officers
  • RAG document retrieval: Grounds decisions in RBI circulars and lending policies
  • Multi-role access: Distinct workflows for loan officers, credit analysts, field officers, underwriters, and administrators

docs.title: Loan Origination Lifecycle
docs.text: CreditShield manages loan applications through a 7-stage lifecycle from initial contact to post-decision handover.

docs.title: Why a Structured Lifecycle Matters
docs.text:
A structured loan origination workflow provides:

  • Consistency: Every application follows the same evaluation process
  • Accountability: Clear ownership at each stage
  • Audit trail: Complete history of decisions and actions
  • Compliance: Systematic enforcement of regulatory requirements
  • Efficiency: Automated steps reduce manual workload

docs.title: Stage 1: Lead and Application Intake
docs.text:
Owner: Loan Officer

What happens:

  • Borrower creates account (mobile or web)
  • Basic profile information collected
  • Loan type and amount requested
  • Initial consent captured for data processing
  • Application Reference Number (ARN) assigned

System actions:

  • Create borrower record in database
  • Generate unique ARN
  • Initialize workflow state
  • Send confirmation notification

Exit criteria: Borrower submits completed application with required profile fields.

docs.title: Stage 2: KYC and Document Collection
docs.text:
Owner: Loan Officer (may coordinate with Field Officer)

What happens:

  • Borrower uploads identity documents (Aadhaar, PAN)
  • Address proof submitted
  • Income documents collected (salary slips, bank statements, ITR)
  • Field Officer may conduct physical verification if required
  • Documents validated for completeness and authenticity

System actions:

  • Store document metadata (file paths, upload timestamps)
  • Run document tampering detection
  • Flag incomplete or suspicious documents
  • Update workflow status to verification pending/completed

Exit criteria: All required documents uploaded and validated. KYC status marked complete.

docs.title: Stage 3: Eligibility and Rule Screening
docs.text:
Owner: System (automated) + Credit Analyst (manual review if needed)

What happens:

  • Backend and AI agent run 50+ underwriting rules
  • Income summary generated
  • Fraud signals detected and flagged
  • Hard rule violations cause auto-reject
  • Soft rule violations trigger manual review

System actions:

  • Execute income analysis tool
  • Execute fraud analysis tool
  • Execute rule violation tool
  • Generate preliminary risk assessment
  • Flag applications with hard-stop conditions

Exit criteria: Rule screening complete. Applications with hard rule violations marked for rejection. Applications with soft rule violations escalated to Credit Analyst.

docs.title: Stage 4: Credit Analysis
docs.text:
Owner: Credit Analyst

What happens:

  • Credit Analyst reviews borrower profile
  • AI agent provides explainable risk rationale
  • Bureau data (if available) evaluated
  • Income stability assessed
  • Counterfactual improvements identified
  • Analyst proposes recommendation (approve/reject/rework)

System actions:

  • Generate 4-page appraisal report
  • Retrieve relevant RBI circulars and policies via RAG
  • Present AI analysis with confidence scores
  • Record analyst recommendation with rationale

Exit criteria: Credit Analyst submits recommendation with documented rationale.

docs.title: Stage 5: Underwriting Decision
docs.text:
Owner: Underwriter (typically Branch Manager)

What happens:

  • Underwriter reviews Credit Analyst recommendation
  • Final policy and risk assessment performed
  • Portfolio fit evaluated
  • Decision options: sanction, conditional sanction, reject, send back for clarification
  • Approval conditions specified if conditional sanction

System actions:

  • Present complete application history and audit trail
  • Display all rule violations and AI analysis
  • Record final decision with conditions
  • Update application status

Exit criteria: Underwriter issues final decision. Status updated to sanctioned, conditionally sanctioned, or rejected.

docs.title: Stage 6: Offer and Acceptance
docs.text:
Owner: Loan Officer

What happens:

  • Approved terms and conditions published to borrower
  • Borrower reviews offer details (amount, tenure, interest rate, EMI)
  • Borrower selects offer and submits acceptance
  • Final consent and agreement signed
  • Terms locked for disbursal

System actions:

  • Generate loan agreement document
  • Send offer notification to borrower
  • Capture borrower acceptance timestamp
  • Update status to offer accepted

Exit criteria: Borrower accepts offer and signs loan agreement.

docs.title: Stage 7: Post-Decision Handover
docs.text:
Owner: System Admin + Loan Officer

What happens:

  • Application data handed over to disbursal system (external or integrated)
  • Borrower and operations teams notified of next steps
  • Tracker updated with disbursal timeline
  • Case closed in Loan Origination System workflow

System actions:

  • Mark workflow as complete
  • Archive application data
  • Maintain read-only audit trail
  • Continue tracker visibility for borrower

Exit criteria: Application transitioned to downstream disbursal/onboarding system.

docs.title: Loan Officer
docs.text:
• Stage 1: Capture application with minimum quality standards
  • Stage 2: Ensure document completeness, coordinate with borrower for missing items
  • Stage 6: Communicate offer terms and assist with acceptance
  • Stage 7: Notify borrower of next steps

docs.title: Field Officer
docs.text:
• Stage 2: Conduct on-ground verification of residence, business, or employment
  • Stage 2: Upload field observations to support underwriting

docs.title: Credit Analyst
docs.text:
• Stage 3: Manual review of soft rule violations
  • Stage 4: Validate AI outputs, perform financial assessment, submit recommendation

docs.title: Underwriter (Branch Manager)
docs.text: • Stage 5: Final credit decision with policy compliance confirmation

docs.title: System Admin
docs.text:
• All stages: Monitor access control, audit logs, workflow health
  • Stage 7: Oversee handover to downstream systems

docs.title: Workflow Status Values
docs.text:
Applications progress through these status values:

Status Stage Meaning draft 1 Application started but not submitted submitted 1 Application submitted, awaiting KYC kyc_pending 2 KYC documents required kyc_complete 2 KYC validation passed screening 3 Automated rule screening in progress manual_review 3-4 Soft rule violations flagged for analyst review analysis 4 Credit Analyst performing assessment underwriting 5 Underwriter reviewing for final decision sanctioned 5 Approved unconditionally conditional_sanction 5 Approved with conditions rejected 3-5 Application rejected (can occur at multiple stages) offer_pending 6 Offer sent, awaiting borrower acceptance offer_accepted 6 Borrower accepted offer closed 7 Workflow complete, handed over

docs.title: Decision Points
docs.text:
The lifecycle includes three major decision points:

  1. Stage 3: Hard rule violations cause automatic rejection (no human intervention)
  2. Stage 4: Credit Analyst recommendation determines whether application proceeds to underwriting
  3. Stage 5: Underwriter final decision determines sanction or rejection

docs.title: Typical Timeline
docs.text:
Stage Duration (Business Days) 1. Application Intake 0-1 2. KYC and Documents 1-3 3. Eligibility Screening 0 (automated) 4. Credit Analysis 1-2 5. Underwriting Decision 1 6. Offer and Acceptance 1-3 7. Post-Decision Handover 0-1 Total 4-11

Timelines vary based on document completeness, field verification requirements, and manual review complexity.

docs.title: Escalation Rules
docs.text:
• Applications stuck in any stage for more than 5 business days trigger escalation alerts
  • Multiple soft rule violations escalate to senior underwriter
  • Fraud signals escalate immediately regardless of stage

docs.title: Rework Loops
docs.text:
Underwriters can send applications back to earlier stages:

  • Back to Credit Analyst for additional analysis
  • Back to Loan Officer for document clarification
  • Back to Field Officer for re-verification

Rework loops are logged in audit trail with reason codes.

docs.title: Parallel Processing
docs.text:
Stages 2 and 3 can overlap:

  • Rule screening begins as soon as minimum document set available
  • KYC validation can continue while preliminary screening runs

docs.title: CreditShield Overview
docs.text: CreditShield is an end-to-end digital lending platform for loan origination and risk decision support.

docs.title: What CreditShield Is
docs.text:
CreditShield manages the complete journey from loan application submission to final underwriting decision. The platform combines automated rule enforcement, AI-powered risk analysis, and human oversight to help lenders process applications faster while maintaining credit quality and regulatory compliance.

The system serves two primary audiences:

  • Borrowers interact through mobile and web interfaces to submit applications, upload documents, and track progress
  • Lending staff (loan officers, credit analysts, field officers, underwriters, administrators) use the web dashboard to review applications, validate information, and make credit decisions

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text: CreditShield consists of four main components:

docs.title: Backend API
docs.text:
Technology: FastAPI + PostgreSQL

The backend manages:

  • User authentication (JWT tokens)
  • Borrower authentication and profiles
  • Application workflow state
  • Document storage metadata
  • API layer for all system operations

See API Endpoints for the complete endpoint list.

docs.title: AI Agent Layer
docs.text:
Technology: Python ReAct agent + AWS Bedrock (Llama 3 70B) + FAISS

The AI agent provides:

  • Explainable credit risk analysis
  • Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) over RBI circulars and lending policies
  • Fraud detection and income verification
  • Rule violation reporting with regulatory citations
  • Counterfactual recommendations (what borrowers can change to qualify)
  • 4-page professional appraisal reports

The agent architecture uses tool calling to perform specific analysis tasks. See RAG Grounding for details on how the agent retrieves policy documents.

docs.title: Web Dashboard
docs.text:
Technology: React + Vite

Internal operations interface for lending staff. Provides role-specific views and workflows for:

  • Loan officers: application intake, document review, borrower communication
  • Credit analysts: financial assessment, AI output validation, recommendation submission
  • Field officers: verification task assignment, on-ground observation upload
  • Underwriters: final decision-making with policy compliance checks
  • System admins: user management, access control, audit logs

docs.title: Mobile Application
docs.text:
Technology: Flutter

Borrower-facing interface for:

  • Account creation and login
  • KYC document upload
  • Loan application submission
  • Offer selection
  • Application status tracking
  • Notifications

docs.title: How the Components Work Together
docs.text:
1. Borrower submits application through mobile app
  2. Backend API stores application and triggers workflow
  3. AI agent runs automated rule checks and generates risk analysis
  4. Lending staff review application and AI outputs through web dashboard
  5. Field officer (if needed) completes physical verification
  6. Credit analyst validates analysis and submits recommendation
  7. Underwriter makes final decision
  8. Backend updates application status and notifies borrower

docs.title: Automated Rule Enforcement
docs.text: 50+ configurable underwriting rules organized across 5 risk categories automatically evaluate every application. Hard rules cause auto-reject. Soft rules trigger manual review. See Underwriting Rules.

docs.title: Explainable AI Decisions
docs.text:
Every AI-generated recommendation includes:

  • Clear rationale with specific data points
  • Regulatory citations from RBI circulars and lending policies
  • Confidence level for the recommendation
  • Counterfactual suggestions for improvement

docs.title: Dual Validation
docs.text: AI outputs undergo validation and auto-correction across retry rounds before presentation to human reviewers.

docs.title: Audit Trail
docs.text:
Complete workflow history retained for every application:

  • Who performed each action
  • When the action occurred
  • What decision was made
  • Why the decision was made (captured rationale)

docs.title: Mock Mode
docs.text: Developers can run the full system without AWS credentials. Mock mode simulates all AWS Bedrock interactions for testing and development. See Configure AWS Bedrock.

docs.title: Supported Loan Types
docs.text:
CreditShield handles multiple loan products with product-specific rules:

  • Personal loans
  • Education loans
  • Business loans
  • Micro loans
  • Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL)

docs.title: Regulatory Compliance
docs.text:
The platform grounds decisions in:

  • RBI Master Direction on Digital Lending (2022)
  • Internal credit policies
  • Lender-specific underwriting guidelines

RAG retrieval ensures every rule violation cites the relevant regulatory source. See RAG Grounding.

docs.title: Deployment Options
docs.text:
CreditShield supports:

  • Local development (see Run CreditShield Locally)
  • Docker containers (docker-compose provided)
  • Kubernetes orchestration (manifests available in repository)

docs.title: What CreditShield Does Not Do
docs.text:
• Post-disbursal loan servicing: Repayment tracking and collections are handled by downstream systems
  • Credit bureau integration: CIBIL scores and bureau data must be obtained through external integrations
  • Payment gateway integration: Disbursal and repayment processing require separate payment system integration
  • Automatic model retraining: ML models are trained offline and deployed manually

docs.title: RAG Grounding
docs.text: CreditShield uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to ground AI decisions in RBI circulars, lending policies, and borrower documents.

docs.title: What RAG Does
docs.text:
RAG combines document retrieval with large language model (LLM) generation. Instead of relying solely on the LLM's training data, the system:

  1. Searches relevant documents for the query
  2. Retrieves the most relevant text chunks
  3. Provides those chunks as context to the LLM
  4. Instructs the LLM to answer based only on the provided context

This approach provides three benefits:

  • Accuracy: Answers grounded in specific policy documents rather than general knowledge
  • Citations: Every answer includes source document references
  • Control: Responses restricted to approved policy sources, preventing hallucination

docs.title: Document Ingestion
docs.text:
Policy documents are processed during system setup:

  1. Split: Documents divided into chunks of 300-500 tokens with small overlap
  2. Embed: Each chunk converted to a numerical vector (embedding) representing its semantic meaning
  3. Index: Embeddings stored in FAISS vector database for fast similarity search
  4. Metadata: Source file, document type, and section heading tracked for each chunk

Document sources:

  • RBI circulars (RBI Master Direction on Digital Lending 2022, KYC guidelines)
  • Internal credit policies
  • Lending product specifications
  • Regulatory compliance documents

docs.title: Query Time Retrieval
docs.text:
When the AI agent needs policy information:

  1. User query or tool call: Example: "Why was HR-01 violated?"
  2. Query embedding: Question converted to same vector format as document chunks
  3. Similarity search: FAISS finds top-k most semantically similar chunks (typically k=3-5)
  4. Context assembly: Retrieved chunks combined into context for LLM
  5. Generation: LLM generates answer restricted to retrieved context only

docs.title: Embedding Models
docs.text:
CreditShield supports two embedding backends:

AWS Bedrock Titan Embed Text v2 (amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0)

  • Cloud-hosted model
  • High quality semantic embeddings
  • Requires AWS credentials
  • Default for production

Local sentence-transformers (all-MiniLM-L6-v2)

  • Runs locally without cloud dependency
  • Faster for development
  • Smaller model, slightly lower quality
  • Used in mock mode

docs.title: Policy RAG
docs.text:
Policy RAG retrieves lending regulations and underwriting rules.

Namespace: policy_global

When used:

  • Rule violation tool needs regulatory citation
  • Credit analyst asks policy questions ("What does RBI say about FOIR limits?")
  • Counterfactual tool suggests improvements ("How can borrower qualify?")

Example query to embedding:

"HR-01 FOIR 65 percent maximum unsecured personal loan obligations income"

Retrieved context (example):

"Fixed Obligations to Income Ratio (FOIR) should not exceed 65% for unsecured personal loans as per internal credit policy aligned with RBI Master Direction on Digital Lending 2022 Section 4.3 on affordability assessment."

Source document: rbi_digital_lending_2022.txt

LLM output with citation:

"HR-01 violation: FOIR 70% exceeds the maximum threshold of 65% for unsecured personal loans. Regulatory reference: RBI Master Direction — Digital Lending (2022) Section 4.3 requires affordability assessment ensuring EMI burden does not exceed borrower capacity. Source: rbi_digital_lending_2022.txt"

docs.title: Borrower Document RAG
docs.text:
Borrower document RAG retrieves information from uploaded loan application documents.

Namespace: borrower_{ARN} (unique per application)

When used:

  • Income verification tool searches salary slips
  • Fraud detection tool analyzes bank statements
  • Credit analyst searches for specific transaction or detail

Document types:

  • Salary slips
  • Bank statements
  • Income Tax Returns (ITR)
  • Employment letters
  • Address proofs
  • Business financial statements

Example query:

"Salary credit from ACME Pvt Ltd in last 6 months"

Retrieved context:

"Bank statement March 2026: Credit ₹75,000 from ACME PVT LTD on 2026-03-01. Bank statement April 2026: Credit ₹75,000 from ACME PVT LTD on 2026-04-01. [Similar entries for 4 more months]"

LLM output:

"Borrower receives consistent monthly salary credits of ₹75,000 from ACME Pvt Ltd. Credits appear on 1st of every month for 6 consecutive months (Nov 2025 - April 2026), indicating stable salaried employment."

docs.title: Retrieval Strategies
docs.text: CreditShield uses multiple retrieval strategies for robustness:

docs.title: 1. Semantic Search (Primary)
docs.text:
Vector similarity search using embeddings. Finds chunks with similar meaning to the query, even if exact words differ.

Advantage: Handles paraphrasing and conceptual questions.

Example: Query "income requirements" retrieves chunks about "minimum monthly salary", "earnings threshold", "compensation criteria".

docs.title: 2. Keyword Search (Fallback)
docs.text:
Text-based search for exact term matches.

When used: Semantic search returns no results (embedding quality issue or very specific term).

Example: Query "HR-01" retrieves chunks containing exact string "HR-01".

docs.title: 3. Hybrid Search
docs.text:
Combine semantic and keyword results, deduplicate, and rank by relevance score.

Advantage: Balances semantic understanding with term precision.

docs.title: RAG Configuration
docs.text:
Tunable parameters (environment variables):

Variable Default Description RAG_TOP_K 3 Number of chunks to retrieve per query RAG_CHUNK_SIZE 400 Target chunk size in tokens RAG_CHUNK_OVERLAP 50 Token overlap between adjacent chunks BEDROCK_EMBEDDING_MODEL amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0 Embedding model ID VECTOR_STORE in_memory in_memory or pgvector (pgvector not yet implemented)

See Configuration Reference for complete list.

docs.title: Handling "I Don't Know"
docs.text:
When retrieved context does not contain the answer, the LLM is instructed to decline instead of guessing.

Example:

Query: "What is the maximum loan tenure for home loans?"

Retrieved context: [Chunks about personal loan FOIR limits, no home loan information]

LLM output:

"I don't have information about home loan tenure limits in the available policy documents. The closest topic I found covers personal loan FOIR requirements. Please consult the home loan policy document or contact the credit policy team."

This prevents hallucination where the LLM invents plausible but false answers.

docs.title: RAG in the 4-Page Appraisal Report
docs.text:
The professional appraisal report uses RAG extensively:

  • Page 1 (Risk Drivers): Retrieves policy citations for each identified risk
  • Page 3 (Liability Analysis): Retrieves FOIR thresholds and loan burden policies
  • Page 4 (Recommendations): Retrieves eligibility criteria for alternative loan products

Every risk driver and recommendation includes a source citation retrieved via RAG.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Typical retrieval latency:

  • Semantic search: 50-100ms for top-3 from 500 document index (in-memory FAISS)
  • Embedding generation: 100-200ms per query (AWS Bedrock Titan)
  • Total RAG round-trip: 150-300ms

Optimization:

  • Pre-compute embeddings during document ingestion (one-time cost)
  • Use in-memory FAISS for sub-100ms search
  • Cache frequently retrieved chunks (TODO: not yet implemented)

docs.title: Document Chunking Strategy
docs.text:
Why chunk: LLMs have context window limits. Chunking allows relevant excerpts to fit in context instead of entire documents.

Chunk size: 300-500 tokens balances:

  • Large chunks: More context per chunk, but fewer chunks fit in LLM window
  • Small chunks: More chunks retrieved, but each may lack context

Overlap: 50-token overlap ensures sentences spanning chunk boundaries are not split.

Splitting method: Split by heading or paragraph boundaries, not mid-sentence.

docs.title: RAG Tools in AI Agent
docs.text: The AI agent uses RAG through two tools:

docs.title: 1. Policy RAG Tool
docs.text:
Tool name: search_policy_documents

Input: Query string (e.g., "FOIR limit for unsecured loans")

Output: Top-k policy chunks with source citations

Use case: Retrieve regulatory basis for underwriting rules

docs.title: 2. Document RAG Tool
docs.text:
Tool name: search_borrower_documents

Input: Application Reference Number (ARN), query string

Output: Top-k chunks from borrower-uploaded documents

Use case: Verify income sources, analyze transaction patterns, check employment continuity

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
RAG has known limitations:

  • Query quality matters: Vague queries retrieve irrelevant chunks. Specific queries with key terms work best.
  • Chunk boundary issues: Answers spanning multiple chunks may be incomplete if chunks not retrieved together.
  • Semantic drift: Embeddings may miss domain-specific jargon or rare terms. Hybrid search mitigates this.
  • No reasoning: RAG retrieves existing text but cannot infer conclusions not stated in documents.

docs.title: Security and Privacy
docs.text:
• Policy documents: Public RBI circulars and internal policies only. No borrower data.
  • Borrower documents: Isolated per ARN. Namespace ensures one borrower cannot access another's documents.
  • Embedding privacy: AWS Bedrock embeddings are not stored by AWS. Vectors stored locally in FAISS.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Planned RAG improvements:

  • Pgvector backend: Persistent vector storage in PostgreSQL for production scale
  • Multi-level indexing: Separate indices for different document types (RBI vs internal policy)
  • Reranking: Second-stage model reranks top-k chunks for precision
  • Semantic caching: Cache embeddings for frequently asked questions

docs.title: Underwriting Rules
docs.text: CreditShield enforces 50+ configurable underwriting rules across 5 risk categories to automate policy compliance and risk assessment.

docs.title: What Underwriting Rules Do
docs.text:
Underwriting rules systematically evaluate loan applications against lender policy and regulatory requirements. Each rule tests a specific condition (income threshold, debt ratio, CIBIL score) and returns a pass or fail result.

Rules provide three benefits:

  1. Consistency: Every application evaluated against identical criteria
  2. Speed: Automated rule execution completes in seconds
  3. Auditability: Rule violations documented with regulatory citations

docs.title: Hard Rules
docs.text:
Hard rules cause automatic rejection when violated. No manual override allowed.

Use case: Violations indicate unacceptable risk or regulatory non-compliance.

Example: A borrower with CIBIL score 480 violates HR-06 (minimum 550 for unsecured personal loans). The application auto-rejects without reaching credit analyst review.

docs.title: Soft Rules
docs.text:
Soft rules trigger manual review when violated. Credit Analyst or Underwriter can approve with documented rationale.

Use case: Violations indicate elevated risk but may be acceptable with compensating factors.

Example: A borrower with income variability 35% violates SR-01 (threshold 30%). Credit Analyst reviews income sources and may approve if variability is seasonal and predictable.

docs.title: 1. Income Stability
docs.text:
Evaluates income source reliability and consistency.

Example rules: - Minimum income threshold per loan product - Income variability coefficient limit - Income verification vs declared variance - Continuous employment duration requirement

Why it matters: Stable income indicates ability to service debt over loan tenure.

docs.title: 2. Credit Behaviour
docs.text:
Assesses past credit usage and repayment patterns.

Example rules: - Minimum CIBIL score threshold - No NPA (Non-Performing Asset) or write-off in last 36 months - Maximum enquiries in last 90 days - No active disputes with lenders

Why it matters: Past credit behaviour predicts future repayment likelihood.

docs.title: 3. Financial Discipline
docs.text:
Measures expense management and savings habits.

Example rules: - Minimum savings ratio (monthly income minus expenses) - Maximum overdraft frequency - Minimum average bank balance - Liquidity stress threshold

Why it matters: Financial discipline indicates borrower ability to absorb income shocks.

docs.title: 4. Loan Burden
docs.text:
Calculates total debt relative to income.

Example rules: - FOIR (Fixed Obligations to Income Ratio) maximum 65% for unsecured personal loans - Maximum number of active loans - Loan stacking detection (3+ new loans in 90 days) - Total EMI to income ratio

Why it matters: Excessive loan burden reduces repayment capacity and increases default risk.

docs.title: 5. Lifestyle Risk
docs.text:
Identifies spending patterns indicating unsustainable lifestyle.

Example rules: - Discretionary spending as percentage of income - Luxury goods transaction frequency - High-value cash withdrawal patterns - Gambling or speculative activity detection

Why it matters: Lifestyle risk can consume income needed for EMI payments.

docs.title: Key Hard Rules
docs.text: The following hard rules are confirmed in the codebase:

docs.title: HR-01: FOIR Maximum
docs.text:
Rule: Fixed Obligations to Income Ratio must not exceed 65% for unsecured personal loans.

Calculation: (Total Monthly EMI Obligations / Monthly Income) × 100

Example violation: Borrower earns ₹50,000/month with existing EMIs totaling ₹35,000/month. FOIR = 70%. Violates HR-01.

Regulatory basis: RBI Master Direction on Digital Lending, internal credit policy.

docs.title: HR-02: Document Tampering
docs.text:
Rule: No document tampering detected in salary slips, bank statements, or ITR.

Detection method: AI fraud analysis tool checks for altered amounts, modified dates, inconsistent fonts, digital manipulation artifacts.

Example violation: Bank statement shows signs of PDF editing. Transaction amounts modified. Violates HR-02.

docs.title: HR-03: NPA/Write-off History
docs.text:
Rule: No NPA or write-off in last 36 months as borrower or guarantor.

Data source: Credit bureau reports, internal lender history.

Example violation: Borrower defaulted on personal loan 24 months ago. Loan written off by previous lender. Violates HR-03.

docs.title: HR-04: Income Variance
docs.text:
Rule: Verified income must not vary by more than 50% from declared income.

Verification sources: Bank statement credit analysis, salary slip verification, ITR cross-check.

Example violation: Borrower declared monthly income ₹60,000. Bank statement shows average monthly credits ₹35,000. Variance = 42%. Violates HR-04 if threshold is 40%.

docs.title: HR-05: Loan Stacking
docs.text:
Rule: Maximum 3 new unsecured loans in 90-day period.

Detection method: Credit bureau enquiry count, internal application database.

Example violation: Borrower applied for 4 personal loans across 3 lenders in last 75 days. Violates HR-05.

Why it matters: Loan stacking indicates financial distress or fraud.

docs.title: HR-06: Minimum CIBIL Score
docs.text:
Rule: Minimum CIBIL score 550 for unsecured personal loans.

Data source: Credit bureau report.

Example violation: Borrower CIBIL score 520. Violates HR-06.

Note: Threshold varies by loan product. Education loans may accept lower scores.

docs.title: HR-07: Minimum Income
docs.text:
Rule: Verified monthly income must meet or exceed product-specific minimum.

Thresholds (example): - Personal loan: ₹25,000/month - Home loan: ₹40,000/month - Business loan: ₹50,000/month

Example violation: Borrower applies for personal loan with verified income ₹20,000/month. Violates HR-07.

docs.title: SR-01: Income Variability
docs.text:
Rule: Income coefficient of variation (CV) triggers manual review if above threshold.

Calculation: (Standard Deviation of Monthly Income / Mean Monthly Income) × 100

Typical threshold: 30%

Example: Freelancer with monthly income ranging ₹30,000–₹90,000. CV = 35%. Triggers SR-01 for manual review.

Credit Analyst action: Assess if variability is seasonal, project-based, or indicates income instability.

docs.title: How Rules Are Evaluated
docs.text:
1. Trigger point: Stage 3 (Eligibility and Rule Screening) in the loan origination lifecycle
  2. Execution: AI agent rule_violation_tool runs all applicable rules
  3. Data sources: Borrower profile, uploaded documents, credit bureau, bank statement analysis
  4. Output: List of violated rules with triggered values, thresholds, regulatory citations
  5. Action: Hard rules cause auto-reject. Soft rules escalate to Credit Analyst.

docs.title: Rule Configuration
docs.text:
Rules are configurable per loan product and lender policy. Parameters that can be adjusted:

  • Threshold values (FOIR limit, minimum income, CIBIL score)
  • Hard vs soft classification (whether violation auto-rejects)
  • Loan product applicability (rules apply to personal loans only, or all products)
  • Regional variations (different thresholds for metro vs non-metro borrowers)

Configuration location: TODO(verify) — Check ai_agent or Backend service layer for rule definition files.

docs.title: Rule Violation Reports
docs.text:
When a rule is violated, CreditShield generates a report containing:

  • Rule ID: Unique identifier (e.g., HR-01, SR-01)
  • Rule name: Human-readable description
  • Triggered value: Actual value calculated for this borrower
  • Threshold: Policy threshold that was exceeded
  • Detail: Explanation of why violation occurred
  • Regulation reference: Citation from RBI circular or lending policy (retrieved via RAG)
  • Source document: Policy file containing the rule definition
  • Severity: Hard (fatal) or soft (warning)

See RAG Grounding for details on how regulatory citations are retrieved.

docs.title: Counterfactual Analysis
docs.text:
When a rule is violated, the AI agent can generate counterfactual recommendations showing what the borrower could change to pass the rule.

Example counterfactual for HR-01 (FOIR) violation:

"Current FOIR is 70% (₹35,000 EMI / ₹50,000 income). To meet the 65% threshold, either: - Increase verified income to ₹53,850/month, or - Reduce existing EMI obligations by ₹2,500/month (close one existing loan), or - Request lower loan amount reducing new EMI by ₹2,500/month"

See Generate an Appraisal Report for examples.

docs.title: Adding Custom Rules
docs.text: Lenders can add custom rules specific to their portfolio risk appetite. See Add an Underwriting Rule.

docs.title: Regulatory Grounding
docs.text:
Every rule violation cites the relevant regulation or policy:

  • RBI Master Direction: Digital Lending (2022)
  • RBI Guidelines: Credit Bureau reporting, KYC norms
  • Internal Policy: Lender-specific credit policies

Citations are retrieved automatically via RAG from policy documents stored in the document/ directory.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text:
Rule evaluation completes in under 3 seconds for a typical application with:

  • 50+ rules executed
  • 3 months of bank statement data
  • 10+ documents analyzed
  • RAG retrieval for 5-10 policy citations

docs.title: Audit and Compliance
docs.text:
Rule violations are logged for every application:

  • Which rules were evaluated
  • Which rules were violated
  • Threshold values at time of evaluation
  • Whether violation caused rejection or manual review
  • Who overrode soft rule violations (if applicable) with rationale

Audit logs support compliance reporting and model governance.

Range: 100-4096

Higher values: Allow longer responses but increase cost and latency

TEMPERATURE

LLM sampling temperature.

Default: 0.3

Range: 0.0-1.0

  • 0.3: Slight randomness (recommended for factual tasks)

Vector database backend for RAG.

Default: 3

Range: 1-10

Target chunk size in tokens for document splitting.

Default: 400

Range: 100-1000

Optimal range: 300-500 tokens per chunk

Token overlap between adjacent chunks.

Default: 50

Range: 0-200

Purpose: Prevent sentences from being split across chunk boundaries

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Never commit secrets to version control
  2. Use different secrets per environment (dev, staging, production)
  3. Rotate JWT secrets periodically (invalidates existing tokens)
  4. Use IAM roles instead of access keys when running on AWS (EC2, ECS, Lambda)
  5. Restrict database user permissions (no need for superuser access)
  6. Use HTTPS in production (not HTTP)

Solution: Restart API server after changing .env. Confirm .env file in correct directory.

docs.text:
Cause: AWS credentials not set and not using mock mode.

Solution: Set AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, or set MOCK_MODE=true.

docs.title: Mock mode not activating
docs.text:
Cause: AWS credentials present and MOCK_MODE not explicitly set to true.

Solution: Set MOCK_MODE=true explicitly to override credential detection.

docs.title: Add an Underwriting Rule
docs.text: Add a custom underwriting rule to CreditShield's automated policy enforcement.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• CreditShield repository cloned locally
  • Understanding of Underwriting Rules
  • Python development environment set up

docs.title: Rule Design Checklist
docs.text:
Before implementing, define:

  • [ ] Rule ID (format: HR-## for hard rules, SR-## for soft rules)
  • [ ] Rule name (human-readable description)
  • [ ] Threshold value and unit
  • [ ] Calculation method (formula or data source)
  • [ ] Hard vs soft classification (auto-reject or manual review)
  • [ ] Applicable loan products (all products, or specific types)
  • [ ] Regulatory basis (RBI circular, internal policy)

docs.title: 1. Define the rule specification
docs.text:
Create a rule specification document:

rule_id: HR-08
rule_name: Maximum Open Credit Cards
description: Borrower must not have more than 5 active credit cards
threshold: 5
calculation: Count of active credit cards from bureau report
severity: hard
applicable_products:
  - personal_loan
  - education_loan
regulatory_basis: Internal credit policy Section 2.4 on credit exposure limits

docs.title: 2. Add rule logic to data adapter
docs.text:
File: TODO(verify) ai_agent/data_adapter.py or backend service layer

Add rule evaluation method:

def check_max_credit_cards(self, arn: str) -> dict:
    """Check if borrower exceeds maximum credit card limit."""
    borrower_data = self.get_borrower_profile(arn)
    bureau_data = self.get_bureau_report(arn)

    active_cards = bureau_data.get("active_credit_cards", 0)
    threshold = 5

    violation = active_cards > threshold

    return {
        "rule_id": "HR-08",
        "name": "Maximum Open Credit Cards",
        "triggered_value": active_cards,
        "threshold": threshold,
        "violated": violation,
        "detail": f"Borrower has {active_cards} active credit cards, exceeds maximum of {threshold}",
    }

docs.title: 3. Register rule in violation tool
docs.text:
File: ai_agent/tools/rule_violation_tool.py

Add RAG query hint for regulatory citation:

_RULE_ID_RAG_QUERY: dict[str, str] = {
    # ... existing rules ...
    "HR-08": "HR-08 maximum open credit cards limit credit exposure policy",
}

docs.title: 4. Add rule to policy evaluation workflow
docs.text:
File: TODO(verify) Backend service or AI agent orchestrator

Register rule in evaluation list:

UNDERWRITING_RULES = [
    # ... existing rules ...
    "HR-08",  # Maximum Open Credit Cards
]

docs.title: 5. Create regulatory policy document
docs.text:
Add policy text to document/ directory:

File: document/internal_credit_policy.txt

Section 2.4: Credit Exposure Limits

Borrowers applying for unsecured personal or education loans must not maintain more than 5 active credit cards. Excessive credit card holdings indicate potential over-leveraging and credit dependency. This limit aligns with conservative credit risk management practices.

Rule ID: HR-08
Threshold: 5 active credit cards
Action: Automatic rejection if exceeded

docs.title: 6. Ingest policy document into RAG
docs.text:
Run RAG ingestion to index the new policy:

cd ai_agent/rag
python ingest.py --source ../../document/internal_credit_policy.txt

Expected result: Policy document chunked, embedded, and added to FAISS index.

docs.title: 7. Write unit tests
docs.text:
File: ai_agent/tests/test_rules.py

def test_hr08_max_credit_cards_pass():
    """Test HR-08 passes when credit cards below threshold."""
    adapter = MockDataAdapter()
    adapter.set_bureau_data("TEST-001", {"active_credit_cards": 3})

    result = adapter.check_max_credit_cards("TEST-001")

    assert result["violated"] is False
    assert result["triggered_value"] == 3

def test_hr08_max_credit_cards_fail():
    """Test HR-08 fails when credit cards exceed threshold."""
    adapter = MockDataAdapter()
    adapter.set_bureau_data("TEST-002", {"active_credit_cards": 7})

    result = adapter.check_max_credit_cards("TEST-002")

    assert result["violated"] is True
    assert result["triggered_value"] == 7
    assert result["rule_id"] == "HR-08"

docs.title: 8. Run tests
docs.text:
python -m pytest ai_agent/tests/test_rules.py::test_hr08_max_credit_cards_pass -v
python -m pytest ai_agent/tests/test_rules.py::test_hr08_max_credit_cards_fail -v

Expected result: Both tests pass.

docs.title: 9. Test end-to-end with sample application

Create test application:

from ai_agent.pipeline.agent_orchestrator import AgentOrchestrator

orchestrator = AgentOrchestrator()
result = orchestrator.analyse_application(
    arn="TEST-003",
    query="Check rule violations"
)

print(result)

Expected result: HR-08 violation appears in rule violation list if test borrower has >5 credit cards.

docs.title: 10. Document the rule
docs.text:
Add entry to Underwriting Rules documentation:

### HR-08: Maximum Open Credit Cards

**Rule:** Borrower must not have more than 5 active credit cards.

**Data source:** Credit bureau report.

**Example violation:** Borrower has 7 active credit cards. Violates HR-08.

**Why it matters:** Excessive credit cards indicate over-leveraging and credit dependency.

docs.title: Configure AWS Bedrock
docs.text: Enable AWS Bedrock for production AI features including Llama 3 70B LLM and Titan Embeddings.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:

  • AWS CLI configured or access credentials (access key ID and secret key)

docs.title: 1. Enable Bedrock model access in AWS Console
docs.text: Log in to AWS Console and navigate to AWS Bedrock service.

docs.title: 2. Select the ap-south-1 region
docs.text:
CreditShield uses Asia Pacific (Mumbai) ap-south-1 region by default.

Change region in top-right corner of AWS Console.

docs.title: 3. Request model access
docs.text:
Navigate to Model access in the Bedrock console left sidebar.

Click Request model access or Manage model access.

docs.title: 4. Enable Llama 3 70B Instruct
docs.text:
Find Meta Llama 3 70B Instruct in the model list.

Click Request access and accept terms.

Model ID: meta.llama3-70b-instruct-v1:0

docs.title: 5. Enable Titan Embed Text v2
docs.text:
Find Amazon Titan Embed Text v2 in the model list.

Click Request access and accept terms.

Model ID: amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0

docs.title: 6. Wait for sanction
docs.text:
Model access is typically granted within 5-10 minutes for standard AWS accounts.

Check status in Model access page. Status should change from "In progress" to "Access granted".

docs.title: 7. Obtain AWS credentials
docs.text:
Option A: Use AWS CLI configuration (recommended)

If AWS CLI is already configured:

aws configure list

CreditShield will use the default profile credentials automatically.

Option B: Generate access keys

  1. Navigate to IAM in AWS Console
  2. Select your user
  3. Go to Security credentials tab
  4. Click Create access key
  5. Choose Application running outside AWS
  6. Copy the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key

Never commit AWS credentials

Do not commit access keys to version control. Use environment variables only.

docs.title: 8. Configure environment variables
docs.text:
Edit .env file in the AI agent directory:

AWS_REGION=ap-south-1
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=your-access-key-id
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=your-secret-access-key
BEDROCK_MODEL_ID=meta.llama3-70b-instruct-v1:0
BEDROCK_EMBEDDING_MODEL=amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0
MOCK_MODE=false

Replace your-access-key-id and your-secret-access-key with your actual credentials.

Using IAM roles

If running on EC2 or ECS, attach an IAM role with Bedrock permissions instead of using access keys. Leave AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY unset.

python -c "import boto3; client = boto3.client('bedrock-runtime', region_name='ap-south-1'); print('Bedrock client initialized successfully')"

Expected result: "Bedrock client initialized successfully" with no errors.

docs.text:

MAX_TOKENS=2048
TEMPERATURE=0.3

  • TEMPERATURE: Randomness (0.0 = deterministic, 1.0 = creative)

docs.title: Cost Estimation
docs.text:
AWS Bedrock charges per token (input and output).

Llama 3 70B Instruct pricing (as of Nov 2026):

  • Input: $0.00099 per 1000 tokens
  • Output: $0.00132 per 1000 tokens

Titan Embed Text v2 pricing:

  • $0.00002 per 1000 tokens

Typical cost per loan application:

  • LLM tokens: ~3000 input + ~1500 output = $4.95 per 1000 applications
  • Embedding tokens: ~2000 per application = $0.04 per 1000 applications
  • Total: ~$5 per 1000 applications

Use AWS Cost Explorer to monitor actual usage.

docs.title: Model access pending
docs.text:
Cause: Model access not yet sanctioned.

Solution: Wait 5-10 minutes. Refresh Model access page in AWS Console. Contact AWS Support if sanction delayed beyond 24 hours.

docs.title: ResourceNotFoundException
docs.text:
Error message: "Could not resolve model meta.llama3-70b-instruct-v1:0"

Cause: Model not available in selected region, or model ID incorrect.

Solution:

  1. Confirm model ID matches exactly: meta.llama3-70b-instruct-v1:0
  2. Verify region set to ap-south-1 or a region where model is available
  3. Check model access status in AWS Console

docs.title: AccessDeniedException
docs.text:
Error message: "User: arn:aws:iam::123456789:user/myuser is not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeModel"

Cause: IAM permissions insufficient.

Solution: Attach the following policy to your IAM user or role:

{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": [
        "bedrock:InvokeModel",
        "bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream"
      ],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}

docs.text:

Solution:

  1. Configure AWS CLI: aws configure
  2. Or set environment variables explicitly
  3. Or attach IAM role if running on EC2/ECS

  • Bank statement CSV or PDF uploaded for the borrower
  • Loan type and amount specified

docs.title: 2. Call the API endpoint
docs.text:
Endpoint: POST /api/v1/risk/professional-report

Request (multipart/form-data):

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/risk/professional-report \
  -F "loan_type=personal" \
  -F "loan_amount=500000" \
  -F "statement=@bank_statement.csv" \
  -F "rules_path=ai_agent/rules" \
  -F "model_path=loan_appraisal_model/model.pkl" \
  -F "use_bedrock=true" \
  -F "output_format=text"

Parameters:

  • loan_type: personal, education, business, micro, bnpl
  • loan_amount: Requested loan amount in rupees
  • statement: Bank statement file (CSV or PDF)
  • rules_path: Path to underwriting rules directory (TODO: verify location)
  • model_path: Path to ML model file (TODO: verify location)
  • use_bedrock: true to use AWS Bedrock LLM, false for mock
  • output_format: text or html

docs.title: 3. Wait for generation
docs.text:
Report generation takes 10-30 seconds depending on:

  • Bank statement size (number of transactions)
  • Bedrock LLM response time
  • Number of RAG retrievals

Expected response: Plain text or HTML formatted 4-page report.

docs.title: 5. Save the report
docs.text:
Save to file:

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/risk/professional-report \
  -F "loan_type=personal" \
  -F "loan_amount=500000" \
  -F "statement=@bank_statement.csv" \
  -F "use_bedrock=true" \
  -F "output_format=text" \
  > appraisal_report.txt

Or with HTML format:

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/risk/professional-report \
  -F "loan_type=personal" \
  -F "loan_amount=500000" \
  -F "statement=@bank_statement.csv" \
  -F "use_bedrock=true" \
  -F "output_format=html" \
  > appraisal_report.html

docs.title: Use from Python Service Layer
docs.text:
Call programmatically from backend code:

from app.services.loan_appraisal_service import LoanAppraisalService

service = LoanAppraisalService()

# Analyze the loan application
analysis_result = service.analyze_loan(
    loan_type="personal",
    loan_amount=500000,
    statement_path="bank_statement.csv",
    rules_path="ai_agent/rules",
    model_path="loan_appraisal_model/model.pkl",
    use_bedrock=True
)

# Generate professional report
report = service.generate_professional_report(
    analysis_result=analysis_result,
    output_format='text'
)

print(report)

docs.title: Executive Summary (Page 1)
docs.text:
Applicant Profile: Classifies borrower as Student, Salaried, Self-employed, or Unemployed based on income patterns.

Financial Health: Rates overall health as Strong, Moderate, or Weak.

Loan Request Overview: Loan type, amount, assumed tenure (24 months), estimated EMI.

Key Financial Snapshot: Income, expenses, savings ratio, inflow vs outflow, liquidity stress.

Top Risk Drivers: 4-6 major risks with explanations.

Final Credit Decision: - Risk Level: LOW / MODERATE / HIGH - Recommendation: APPROVE / APPROVE_WITH_CAUTION / REJECT - Confidence Level: HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW - Final Score: X/100

Decision Justification: Why the recommendation was made.

docs.title: Income & Cashflow (Page 2)
docs.text:
Income Analysis: Source identification, stability, monthly estimate, trend, risks.

Cashflow Analysis: 12-month inflow/outflow, net savings, savings ratio interpretation.

Liquidity Analysis: Min/max/average balance, liquidity stress, stress days, month-end stress.

Financial Discipline: Spending vs earning behavior, consistency, volatility.

docs.title: Expense & Liability (Page 3)
docs.text:
Expense Behavior: Essential spending breakdown (rent, food, travel, bills), discretionary spending, lifestyle insight.

Liability Analysis: Existing EMIs, BNPL/credit usage, hidden liabilities, Fixed Obligations to Income Ratio, annual debt payment.

Loan Affordability: - Expected monthly EMI - EMI-to-income ratio - Current surplus - Expected surplus after new EMI - Classification: AFFORDABLE / RISKY / NOT_AFFORDABLE - Detailed rationale

  • RAG policy retrieval: Accurate regulatory citations require well-indexed policy documents

docs.title: Run CreditShield Locally
docs.text: Set up CreditShield development environment and run the backend API locally.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or later
  • PostgreSQL 14 or later
  • Git
  • pip (Python package manager)

docs.title: 1. Clone the repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Yash-Kalkhambkar/Credshield.git
cd Credshield

docs.title: 2. Set up the backend
docs.text:
Navigate to the Backend directory:

cd Backend

docs.title: 3. Create a virtual environment
docs.text: python -m venv venv

docs.title: 4. Activate the virtual environment
docs.text:
On Linux/macOS:

source venv/bin/activate

On Windows (PowerShell):

.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

On Windows (Command Prompt):

venv\Scripts\activate.bat

docs.title: 5. Install Python dependencies
docs.text: pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: 6. Configure environment variables
docs.text:
Copy the example environment file:

cp .env.example .env

Edit .env and configure the following required variables:

DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:password@localhost:5432/creditshield
JWT_SECRET_KEY=your-secret-key-here
SYSTEM_ADMIN_USERNAME=system_admin
SYSTEM_ADMIN_PASSWORD=Admin@123

Replace user, password, and database name with your PostgreSQL credentials.

Generate a secure JWT secret

Generate a random secret key for JWT_SECRET_KEY. Do not use the example value in production.

python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(32))"

See Configuration Reference for all available environment variables.

docs.title: 7. Verify database connectivity
docs.text:
Start the API server in development mode:

uvicorn app.main:app --reload

Database tables not auto-created

CreditShield does not create database tables at startup. The above command starts the API but the database remains empty until migrations are run or tables are created manually.

docs.title: 8. Test the health endpoint
docs.text:
Open a browser or use curl:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health/db

Expected response: JSON indicating database connection status.

docs.title: 9. View API documentation
docs.text:
Navigate to http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs in your browser.

Expected result: Interactive OpenAPI (Swagger) documentation displaying all available endpoints.

docs.title: 10. Test authentication
docs.text:
Use the system admin credentials to obtain a JWT token:

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/v1/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"username":"system_admin","password":"Admin@123"}'

Expected response: JSON with access_token field.

docs.title: Optional: Set Up AI Agent in Mock Mode
docs.text: To test AI features without AWS credentials:

docs.title: 1. Navigate to the AI agent directory
docs.text:
cd ../ai_agent

(Or from repository root: cd "Design Loan Origination Dashboard/ai_agent" — path differs based on directory structure)

docs.title: 2. Install AI agent dependencies
docs.text: pip install -r requirements-agent.txt

docs.title: 3. Enable mock mode
docs.text:
On Linux/macOS:

export MOCK_MODE=true

On Windows (PowerShell):

$env:MOCK_MODE="true"

docs.title: 4. Run AI agent tests
docs.text:
python -m pytest tests -v

Expected result: All tests pass. AI agent uses mock LLM and embeddings instead of AWS Bedrock.

docs.title: Verify the Setup
docs.text:
Confirm the following:

  • [ ] Backend API running at http://127.0.0.1:8000
  • [ ] OpenAPI docs accessible at /docs
  • [ ] Database health check returns success
  • [ ] JWT token generated successfully with system admin credentials
  • [ ] AI agent tests pass in mock mode (if set up)

docs.title: Connection refused when accessing API
docs.text:
Cause: API server not running or using wrong port.

Solution: Confirm uvicorn command completed without errors. Check that port 8000 is not in use by another application.

docs.title: Database connection error
docs.text:
Cause: PostgreSQL not running or credentials incorrect.

Solution:

  1. Verify PostgreSQL service is running: 

    pg_isready

  2. Confirm credentials in .env match your PostgreSQL setup.

  3. Ensure database exists. Create if needed: 

    CREATE DATABASE creditshield;

docs.title: Import errors when running tests
docs.text:
Cause: PYTHONPATH not set for AI agent tests.

Solution: Set PYTHONPATH before running pytest:

On Linux/macOS:

export PYTHONPATH=.

On Windows (PowerShell):

$env:PYTHONPATH="."

Then re-run: python -m pytest ai_agent/tests -v

docs.title: JWT token invalid or expired
docs.text:
Cause: JWT_SECRET_KEY mismatch between token generation and validation.

Solution: Ensure .env file loaded correctly. Restart API server after changing .env.

docs.title: Security Notes
docs.text:
• Never commit .env file to version control
  • Use strong passwords for system admin account in production
  • Generate unique JWT_SECRET_KEY per environment
  • Use HTTPS in production, not HTTP
